situation: A regional gym chain's profit fell 20% this year. Revenue is flat, and you've just found that costs rose $2M, almost all of it in the 6 newest clubs.
new_fact: The 6 newest clubs opened in the last 18 months; the older clubs' costs per member are flat.
model_answer_stage1: Compare cost per member at the 6 new clubs with the older ones, by cost line, because the $2M rise sits almost entirely in the new clubs.
model_answer_stage2: Keep: older clubs' costs per member are flat, so the rise really is in the new clubs, and comparing their cost lines shows which cost drives it.
